panels.title: Disk used (amber 75%, red 85%)
panels.description:
The VME manager stores its database (MySQL), OpenSearch/Elasticsearch data (logs and stats),
RabbitMQ queues, uploaded images and local backups on its disk, mostly under `/var/opt/morpheus`.

| Used | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **under 75%** | Healthy |
| **75 to 85%** | Plan: find what's growing (usually `elasticsearch`, `bitcan/backups` or `morpheus-ui/vms`) |
| **over 85%** | Act now. HPE: with the partition 85% full or more, Elasticsearch enters an unhealthy state and the appliance won't function properly ([requirements](https://github.com/HewlettPackard/morpheus-docs/blob/dev-9.1/getting_started/requirements/requirements.rst)). |

To free space: lower **Stats Retainment** (Administration > Settings > Appliance) or the log **Availability Time Frame**
(Administration > Settings > Monitoring), move backups to a Storage Provider, or grow the manager's disk. HPE doesn't publish a disk size for the VM Essentials manager; it comes with the QCOW2 image the manager is deployed from.

targets.rawSql: SELECT max((f->>'percent')::numeric) FROM appliance a, jsonb_array_elements(a.health->'storage'->'files') f WHERE a.id = 1

panels.title: Manager size: Essentials and Enterprise
panels.description:
How this manager compares with both HPE sizing guides, each with its own result.

**VM Essentials** (applies to a VME manager): the HPE Morpheus Manager Installer and `hvmcli deploy` create the manager
from the VME QCOW2 image with a sizing profile: **Small = 12 GB RAM, 2 vCPUs**; **Medium** (the `hvmcli` default) and
**Large** are bigger, but HPE doesn't publish their values or a manager disk size ([installer](https://github.com/HewlettPackard/morpheus-docs/blob/dev-9.1/getting_started/installation/singleNode/hpe_installer.rst)).
HPE publishes no per-manager object limits and asks for a workload-specific sizing review before large deployments
([maximums](https://github.com/HewlettPackard/morpheus-docs/blob/dev-9.1/infrastructure/clusters/hvm/maximums.rst)).

**Morpheus Enterprise** (for reference, e.g. before moving to an Enterprise license): the appliance requirements are
**16 GB RAM, 4 cores, 200 GB disk** ([requirements](https://github.com/HewlettPackard/morpheus-docs/blob/dev-9.1/getting_started/requirements/requirements.rst)).

Memory allows 1 GB for what the OS doesn't report. Sustained CPU pressure, high JVM memory or swap use on this
dashboard are the signs to move up a profile.

targets.rawSql: WITH m AS (SELECT DISTINCT ON (metric) metric, value FROM metrics WHERE entity_type = 'appliance' AND metric IN ('cpu.processorCount', 'memory.systemMemory', 'storage.total') AND time > now() - INTERVAL '1 hour' ORDER BY metric, time DESC), c AS (SELECT (SELECT value FROM m WHERE metric = 'cpu.processorCount') AS cores, (SELECT value FROM m WHERE metric = 'memory.systemMemory') AS mem, (SELECT value FROM m WHERE metric = 'storage.total') AS disk) SELECT r.resource AS "Item", r.have AS "Manager has", r.ess AS "Essentials needs", r.ess_res AS "Essentials result", r.ent AS "Enterprise needs", r.ent_res AS "Enterprise result" FROM (SELECT 1 AS o, 'Overall' AS resource, cores::int || ' vCPUs, ' || pg_size_pretty(mem::bigint) AS have, 'Small profile: 2 vCPUs, 12 GB' AS ess, CASE WHEN cores < 2 OR mem < 11 * 2^30 THEN 'below Small' WHEN cores <= 2 AND mem < 13 * 2^30 THEN 'matches Small' ELSE 'Medium or Large' END AS ess_res, '4 cores, 16 GB, 200 GB' AS ent, CASE WHEN cores >= 4 AND mem >= 15 * 2^30 AND disk >= 200e9 THEN 'meets' ELSE 'below' END AS ent_res FROM c UNION ALL SELECT 2, 'CPU cores', cores::int::text, '2', CASE WHEN cores >= 2 THEN 'meets' ELSE 'below' END, '4', CASE WHEN cores >= 4 THEN 'meets' ELSE 'below' END FROM c WHERE cores IS NOT NULL UNION ALL SELECT 3, 'Memory', pg_size_pretty(mem::bigint), '12 GB', CASE WHEN mem >= 11 * 2^30 THEN 'meets' ELSE 'below' END, '16 GB', CASE WHEN mem >= 15 * 2^30 THEN 'meets' ELSE 'below' END FROM c WHERE mem IS NOT NULL UNION ALL SELECT 4, 'Disk', pg_size_pretty(disk::bigint), 'not published', 'n/a', '200 GB', CASE WHEN disk >= 200e9 THEN 'meets' ELSE 'below' END FROM c WHERE disk IS NOT NULL ) r ORDER BY r.o

panels.title: Host filesystems (node_exporter)
panels.description:
Filesystems on the HVM host itself, from node_exporter (install it with tools/install-exporters.sh).

* **Root (/)** and **/var** hold the OS, logs and libvirt state. A full root filesystem can stop VMs from starting or migrating.
* Local datastores (Directory datastores) live on these filesystems, so they fill up as VM disks grow.
* Shared datastores mounted on the host (NFS, GFS2) appear too, once per host, labeled with their VME datastore name.

Amber at 80%, red at 90%. **Days to full** projects the last 24 hours forward and is blank when usage isn't growing.
**Read-only** usually means the kernel remounted the filesystem after a disk error: investigate straight away.

panels.description: Write latency above ~20 ms slows the manager's database.

targets.rawSql: SELECT DISTINCT ON (task) task AS "Task", time AS "Last run", ok AS "OK", duration_ms AS "ms", items AS "Items", error AS "Error" FROM collector_runs ORDER BY task, time DESC
SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(time, $__interval), task AS metric, avg(duration_ms) AS value FROM collector_runs WHERE $__timeFilter(time) GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1
SELECT time AS "Time", task AS "Task", error AS "Error" FROM collector_runs WHERE NOT ok AND $__timeFilter(time) ORDER BY time DESC LIMIT 50

SELECT 'metrics (raw)' AS "Table", pg_size_pretty(hypertable_size('metrics')) AS "Size", (SELECT count(*) FROM timescaledb_information.chunks WHERE hypertable_name = 'metrics') AS "Chunks" UNION ALL SELECT 'database total', pg_size_pretty(pg_database_size(current_database())), NULL
